clue.text: People of the highest standing reject two prizes

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the two prize words are read from the end backwards

parts.note: a reward is a prize
a pot is a prize, as in a trophy cup or a jackpot

explanation.surface: Some top-class grandee scornfully turns down a pair of awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' turns the whole run REWARD + POT backwards, giving TOP then DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for the upper class, those of the highest social rank.

clue.text: Lukewarm food served up, including pie crust

indicators.note: including means the reversed food word takes the next piece inside it
in a down clue, served up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: diet means food, what one eats

indicators.note: a crust is the outer edge of a pie, taken here as just its first letter

explanation.surface: A tepid meal is brought to the table with a bit of pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns DIET into TEID; 'including' puts P, the first letter of pie, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid and lukewarm are synonyms for only slightly warm.

clue.text: Bit by bit, or bit by bite?

definitions.meaning: gradually, one portion at a time
whimsically, a meal eaten one piece at a time

explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually in stages; the second reading splits it into a piece and a meal.

clue.text: Heavy fall, but right arm is not broken

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone has a nasty fall but is relieved the right arm has not been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like a denial in the surface but is the anagram signal on R, ARM, IS and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a heavy fall of rain, so the phrase fits a torrential storm.

clue.text: Baptist will usually welcome an addition lion to the family

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Baptist will usually welcome an addition lion to the family': the stray word 'lion' is an OCR artefact, the scan is unreadable and a search found no copy of the clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Baptist will usually welcome an addition lion to the family

clue.text: Change will be no good for the spirit

definitions.text: Change will be no good for the spirit

parts.words: Change will be no good for the spirit
parts.note: describes the mischievous sprite of English folklore, a shape-shifter and swapper of babies whose pranks did no good

explanation.surface: Some transformation is going to be bad for the soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The folklore sprite, also called Puck, is known for transformations and mischief; 'spirit' suggests the soul or liquor but means a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: This hobgoblin of English folklore is the mischievous fairy Shakespeare calls Puck.

clue.text: Extra burden laid on bishop

indicators.note: laid on means the burden word is set after the bishop's letter in the across entry

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an onus is a burden or responsibility

explanation.surface: A clergyman is given yet another heavy responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is something extra, given on top of what is due.

clue.text: Wrapping divine purchase for friend

indicators.note: wrapping means the purchase word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine or theologian

explanation.surface: Gift-wrapping a heavenly buy for a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a clergyman, abbreviated DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddy is an informal word for a friend or mate.

clue.text: Under no circumstances featured in LUAUS Alexandrine verse

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Under no circumstances featured in LUAUS Alexandrine verse': the stray word 'LUAUS' is an OCR artefact, the scan is unreadable and a search found no copy of the clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Under no circumstances featured in LUAUS Alexandrine verse

clue.text: Complicated steel part used in explosive

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An intricate steel component is fitted into a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is an ingredient of gunpowder and so is used in explosives.

clue.text: Divine couple given decree

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple
an edict is an official decree

explanation.surface: A pair of people receive an official order from on high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a verb here, to foretell, not an adjective about the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foresee or forecast, which is what predicting means.

clue.text: Torture is base and profoundly immoral

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a bed of concrete or a riverbed
evil means deeply wicked

explanation.surface: Torture is described as a low and utterly wicked act.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to torment or plague someone, a synonym for torture.

clue.text: Line up to put clothes on

definitions.meaning: soldiers ... ranks when they line up straight

explanation.definitionFit: Dress is a military verb for aligning troops and an everyday one for clothing.

clue.text: Make more efficient faction back questionable spying technique

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or refine, making something more effective

indicators.note: back means the faction word is read backwards

parts.note: a party is a political faction

explanation.surface: Streamlining a group is described as a dubious espionage method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the faction word from right to left; 'Make more efficient' is a verb phrase for sharpening, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeytrap uses seduction to compromise a target, an ethically dubious method of espionage.

clue.text: Conservative has to revise statement of beliefs

parts.note: to redo is to revise or do over

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is forced to rewrite a manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revise' looks like an anagram signal but means REDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a set of beliefs someone professes.

clue.text: Constant oscillation is damaging

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for a constant, the speed of light
rippling is a wavelike oscillation of a surface

explanation.surface: Endless shaking is causing serious harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Crippling means severely damaging, as in crippling debts.

clue.text: Programme ruined by bad actors

indicators.note: ruined signals that the letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A show is wrecked by a poor cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a radio or television programme.

clue.text: I stood out no end in dismal scandal

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the dismal word

parts.note: dour means gloomy or dismal

indicators.note: no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: shone means was conspicuous, stood out

explanation.surface: Someone was conspicuous in a miserable scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts SHONE to SHON; I + SHON goes 'in' DOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour is disgrace or shame, which a scandal brings.

clue.text: Heading home, wearing silver in profusion

indicators.note: wearing means the silver symbol is worn around the other pieces

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
bound means heading for, as in homeward bound
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for home dressed in silver finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' means the silver symbol is put on like a garment around the heading and home pieces; 'Heading' is a participle here, not a newspaper headline.
explanation.definitionFit: Abounding means existing in large numbers, plentiful, in profusion.

clue.text: I criticise a poor city

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly
bad means poor in quality

explanation.surface: Someone runs down a poverty-stricken town.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.

clue.text: A number obtain illegal drugs …

explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and to score is slang for buying narcotics.

clue.text: … quickly by appointment, as the criminal …

parts.note: a post is a job or appointment

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is quickly given a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-haste is an adverb meaning with great speed.

clue.text: Part of flower found in South-east China

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
china is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, a pal

explanation.surface: A bloom grown in south-eastern China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but china is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leafy parts that encloses a flower bud.

clue.text: Dog that's strong and well-built

definitions.meaning: a sled dog of the Arctic

explanation.definitionFit: A husky is a sled dog, and husky also describes a big, burly person.

clue.text: … had confessed

explanation.definitionFit: Owned means possessed, and to own a fault is to admit or confess it.

clue.text: Did we ever live thus? Early on

definitions.text: Did we ever live thus? Early on

indicators.note: early on points to the first letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A nostalgic question about whether we really lived like that in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the answer means lived, and the question looks back to how we lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to live somewhere.

clue.text: I am old-fashioned — I permit no further progress

parts.note: I'm is a contraction of I am
passe means out of date

explanation.surface: A fusty conservative declares they will block all progress.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a situation in which no progress can be made.

clue.text: Pope's verse

definitions.meaning: relating to one of the popes named Leo
a medieval Latin metre with internal rhyme

explanation.definitionFit: Leonine describes things of Pope Leo, and leonine verse is a rhymed medieval form.

clue.text: Seabird you at first observed in the Channel …

parts.note: a gull is a seabird

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A seabird seen in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Channel' suggests the sea between England and France, but channel is the definition, a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a narrow channel cut by water.

clue.text: … complete with blue spot on

parts.note: down means sad, blue
right means exactly correct

explanation.surface: Feeling low but exactly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means utter or complete, as in a downright lie.
